note: The durable audit trail for lib/market/fund-name.ts's name-pattern classifier - see lib/market/fund-name-review.ts for how curate-bot-watchlist.ts uses this. Every entry here is a human decision about one symbol the classifier flagged, keyed by symbol. A flagged symbol with no entry here halts the curation script rather than being silently included or excluded - see curate-bot-watchlist.ts's own NEEDS REVIEW handling. Add an entry (decision + a short rationale) for any new symbol the script reports under NEEDS REVIEW, then re-run it.

entries.rationale: Arm Holdings plc - a real Nasdaq-100 semiconductor IP company, listed on Nasdaq via American Depositary Shares (the standard mechanism for a foreign-domiciled company), not a fund product.
PDD Holdings Inc. (Pinduoduo/Temu's parent) - a real Nasdaq-100 e-commerce company, listed via ADS for the same reason as ARM, not a fund.

Invesco Ltd itself - a real S&P 500 asset-management company. It issues funds/ETFs; it is not one of its own funds. The issuer-prefix pattern exists to catch products those firms issue, and correctly also catches the firm's own ticker as a name-collision - a known, expected case, not a surprise.
Northern Trust Corporation - a real S&P 500 bank/asset-custody company. 'Trust' is part of its legal name (a real trust bank), not a fund/trust-vehicle wrapper.
Camden Property Trust - a real S&P 500 REIT. REITs are legally organized as trusts by statute; this is an operating real-estate company, not a pooled investment vehicle.
Essex Property Trust - a real S&P 500 REIT, same reasoning as CPT.
Federal Realty Investment Trust - a real S&P 500 REIT, same reasoning as CPT.
Digital Realty Trust - a real S&P 500 REIT, same reasoning as CPT.
